title: Policy Gradients
interviewAnswer: Policy-gradient methods optimize policy parameters directly. REINFORCE increases the log-probability of actions that produced high return and decreases it for poor return. This handles stochastic and continuous policies naturally, but raw Monte Carlo gradients can have high variance.
why: Policy gradients underpin actor-critic methods and PPO, which are important in control and LLM alignment contexts.
intuition: If an action was followed by a surprisingly good outcome, make that action a little more likely next time in similar states.
deepDive: The policy-gradient theorem gives an expectation of ∇ log π(a|s) weighted by return or advantage. A baseline can reduce variance without changing the expected gradient. Actor-critic methods replace full-episode Monte Carlo return with a learned critic/advantage estimate.
workedExample: A two-action softmax policy receives reward +1 after action A and −1 after B. REINFORCE nudges logits to increase P(A) and decrease P(B).
commonMistakes: Saying policy gradients require a differentiable environment; they differentiate the policy probability, not environment dynamics.
Ignoring variance and the role of baselines/critics.
production: Reward normalization, stable batching, reproducible rollouts and policy constraints matter as much as the gradient formula.

lab.goal: Implement REINFORCE for a two-armed stochastic bandit with a softmax policy.
